description: The span half of the route structures: pieces authored to CARRY a way over a gap, as opposed to route-structures-v1's flights and decks, which carry it up a slope. The gap this fills (owner question 2026-09-09): route-structures-v1's only road-spanning piece is wrbridgestone01, a 4.216 m free-standing slab with riseM 0, no pier, no abutment and no parapet, so a 389.6 m crossing became ~93 slabs floating end to end. The measured distribution says a single-piece bridge cannot answer it either — of the 211 spanning structures the shortest is 23.6 m, the median 70.0 m and the longest 389.6 m, so 69% are longer than the longest whole bridge vanilla ships. What a long crossing needs is a viaduct: a repeating deck on piers, terminated at both ends. Three families, and NOTHING is mixed between them. (1) nordic-viaduct, the vanilla Nordic temple exterior platform-tower system: a deck module, the tower that carries it, the end cap that terminates it, the shaft foot, and the set's own approach stair with its left and right caps. (2) marsh-timber, the Black Marsh & Valenwood hut-exterior causeway: a legged timber span and the three step pieces the same authors used to meet the ground. (3) stone-arch, the four vanilla free-standing landscape bridges plus dragonbridge01 — complete authored bridges, parapets and abutments included, for a crossing short enough that one piece spans it whole. Every offset in snapLogic is the authors' own, mined from the source plugins into world/sources/placement/kit-assemblies-mined.json, not inferred from a name. Consumed by worldgen.compile_route_structures.

snapLogic.families: Three span families, each self-contained. A family names the repeating deck and its measured run, the pier that carries the deck and the authored spacing between piers, the end piece that terminates the run, and where one exists the approach the same authors used to bring the way up to deck level. The compiler picks the family from the region the way runs through and the arrangement from the MEASURED run, never from a piece's name.
snapLogic.nordic-viaduct: Roads and trunk roads over a long crossing. Deck: nortmpextplattowerbridge01, run 5.462 m along the way, 2.873 m wide (narrower than the 4.047 m wrbridgestone01 slab it replaces — a one-cart deck, which is what a viaduct in this set is), 1.479 m thick, pivot at its own mid-length (originOffsetM y = 2.731). The authors self-chained it at exactly 5.46 m end to end (mined vanilla:t0029, n=25) and at 10.92 m where a piece is skipped (t1941, n=3), so the deck's stated module length and its authored spacing agree to a centimetre. Pier: nortmpextplattower01, 3.475 x 5.047 m in plan and 26.825 m tall, its pivot AT DECK LEVEL with 21.848 m of shaft hanging below (originOffsetM z = 21.848) — placed at the deck line it buries itself in shallow ground and stands full height where the ground falls away, which is how the set was built to cross undulating terrain. The authors set a tower 2.73 m from a deck pivot (t0038, n=22), i.e. at a deck joint, giving a pier every one or two deck modules (5.46 m / 10.92 m); the 8.19 m variant (t0412) is the same joint one module further on. nortmpextplattower02 is the wider twin, 7.283 m in plan, pivot centred, for the deeper piers. Foot: nortmpextplatshaftbot01, a 7.283 x 7.283 m base pad, 0.455 m thick, under a tower where the shaft meets ground. End: nortmpextplattowerbridgeendcap01, 0.963 m of run at the deck's own 2.788 m width — the abutment that stops the run instead of leaving a slab hanging. Free deck: nortmpextplattowerbridgefree01, the unsupported 3.731 m variant the authors placed 4.55 m before a deck (t0016, n=31) where a run leaves a platform. Approach: nortmpextplatstairmid02, 10.791 m of run for 7.306 m of rise (34.1 deg, inside the 35 deg flight cap), with nortmpextplatstaircapl01 and staircapr01 set at exactly +/-3.64 m from the stair pivot (t-stairmid02 pairs, n=28 and n=27) to close its two sides.
snapLogic.marsh-timber: Hist-heartland and marsh ways at or near ground level. Deck: bmv:architecture/huts/exterior/bridge01, run 4.977 m, 2.284 m wide, 3.134 m tall WITH ITS OWN LEGS and its pivot on the ground (originOffsetM z = -0.003) — it needs no separate pier because it carries one. CAVEAT, measured and not glossed: the authors' repeated placement of one bridge01 relative to another is 9.70 m (mined bmv-blackmarsh:t0076, n=13), which is 4.72 m MORE than the piece is long. That is two separate spans with a gap between them, not an end-to-end chain — so this piece is a single 4.977 m span, and there is no authored evidence it may be tiled into a longer causeway. Use it whole or not at all. Approach: steps02, the same 2.284 m width and 3.156 m height as the deck, which the authors placed 9.71 m from a bridge01 (t0277, n=3) — the piece that brings the way up to deck level, at the same spacing and with the same gap. steps01 (0.446 m rise) and steps03 (0.566 m rise) are the small ground steps of the same set, for the last lift onto the approach.
snapLogic.stone-arch: A crossing one authored bridge spans whole. bridgeshort01: 23.435 m of span, 7.451 m wide. bridgenarrow01: the same 23.435 m span at 4.832 m, for a track. bridge01: 42.084 m at 9.133 m. bridgelong01: 52.188 m at 9.133 m — the longest single span vanilla ships. All four have their pivot at deck level (originOffsetM z = 14.373) with the arch and abutments hanging ~14.4 m below, so they are placed on the deck line and the arch finds its own springing. dragonbridge01 is the monumental one, 73.321 m of span, 15.05 m wide, 42.839 m tall, pivot 22.43 m above its base: a landmark, placed by hand, never tiled. None of these five chain — no source plugin ever placed two of them end to end — so a span longer than the piece is a job for nordic-viaduct, not for a row of bridges.
snapLogic.unitScale: Bethesda units at 0.014224 m/unit, as everywhere else in the pipeline. sizeM is [x, plan-y, vertical-z] in the built manifest.
snapLogic.anchoring: Deck and bridge pieces are placed by their DECK line, not their foot: nortmpextplattower01, nortmpextplattowerbridge01 and all five stone arches carry their structure below the pivot on purpose. The marsh-timber pieces are the exception and are placed by the foot (originOffsetM z ~ 0).
